items.text: Donald Trump said in a Truth Social message that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and holds hundreds of billions of dollars of Iran's money and controls their strait. He also wrote that he asked JD Vance to focus entirely on corruption and widespread crimes. Reuters reported that Vance has recently been involved in efforts to establish contact with Iran.

A number of political and civil activists issued a joint statement protesting the increase in executions in Iran, especially in political and security cases, and called for an immediate and unconditional halt to executions. They referred to the executions of detainees from the December 1404 protests and violations of fair trial principles. The signatories emphasized that executions neither deter nor help solve problems and called for an immediate stop to executions as a necessary step for realizing civil rights and sustainable security.

The publication of a sale advertisement for Amirhossein Mahmoudi, a young Persepolis player, in a newspaper has been met with protest from Mehdi Tartar, the team's coach. Tartar criticized the advertisement's release without coordination with the coaching staff and intended to return Mahmoudi to group training after a discussion. A Persepolis official said the ad was published for financial transparency and due to the club's stock market status, and it does not mean Mahmoudi's sale is definite.

A court in Britain found Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi-Mansh guilty of aiding the Islamic Republic's intelligence service in spying on two Iran International journalists. Sepahvand was found guilty unanimously on two charges of aiding a foreign intelligence service and intent to carry out a violent attack. Their sentencing is scheduled for December 17 at 14:00 at the Old Bailey court in London.

The Iranian Teachers' Trade Union condemned the widespread issuance of death sentences following the protests of Dey 1404. The statement referred to the killing of a significant number of citizens, especially young people, and described the increase in issuing and carrying out death sentences for detained protesters as a sign of using this punishment as a tool to create fear and suppress society. The union also emphasized the right of young people to have a future full of hope, freedom, and dignified life.

The board of directors of the American company Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as CEO and other managerial roles. Colette Kress, the executive vice president and chief financial officer, has accepted to act as interim head of Nvidia until a new CEO is selected. Huang's resignation was announced after pressure due to the disclosure of two extramarital relationships, including one with a Chinese woman suspected of collaborating with Beijing's intelligence agencies.

Iranian users on social media, amid war and increasing economic pressures, write about fatigue, livelihood uncertainty, and concerns about the possible start of a new round of attacks. Statements by Islamic Republic officials about people's resilience have also faced widespread reactions from users. Adaleh Borang, a member of the Iran International editorial team, talks about these reactions.

Elina Hojati's mother said in a video that her daughter was killed by a "war bullet." She referred to Elina's academic achievements and emphasized she will never forgive the perpetrators of the murder. Elina, a 23-year-old student, was killed by Islamic Republic agents in Tehran on the evening of 18 Dey.

Information received by Iran International indicates that managers and officials of some high schools in Shiraz subject students to extensive body searches. Students say the school staff touch all parts of their bodies during inspections, causing discomfort and embarrassment. Last month, a student from Fazli Technical School in Fardis told Iran International that the school staff touch students' private parts during searches and face harsher treatment if they protest.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic will fail due to Tehran's opposition to withdrawing from its nuclear program. He added that if the siege continues, the Islamic Republic may take actions that could pave the way for another US military attack.

The family of Asieh Ramazani stated in a video and text that their grief and longing continue 10 months after her killing. Asieh, a mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from Islamic Republic forces during the protests on 19 Dey 1404 in Tehran at the age of 39.

The Israeli Prime Minister's office denied reports of a severe verbal dispute between Netanyahu and Trump during a phone call about resuming military attacks on Iran. Netanyahu's office called the news fake and baseless. Sources said the call was tense, but a senior Israeli official said the conversation was not difficult.

Vicky Evans, Deputy Police Commissioner and Senior National Coordinator of the UK Counter-Terrorism Police, said in an exclusive interview with Iran International that evidence presented in court shows the order to carry out this operation was issued by individuals linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

According to Reuters, Nvidia's board is considering removing Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, following reports about his personal relationships and the start of an internal US investigation, and he has resigned from this position. Nvidia's shares fell about seven percent in early Frankfurt trading. These developments coincide with the investigation of a woman named Alice Huang's role in the possible transfer of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and increased pressure from US lawmakers for stricter chip export restrictions to China.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center announced that the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz is "severe" and there is a high likelihood of further attacks on oil tankers and other vessels in the area. Four attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf have been recorded in the past 96 hours. The center warned that the likelihood of more attacks, especially near the coast of Musandam, Oman, is very high.

Police reported a shooting of five people in the Logan Circle area of Washington, about one and a half kilometers from the White House. Police forces are providing the latest information about this incident.

Javad Khaki, a political prisoner, returned to the Central Prison of Karaj after the end of his leave. According to the Harana news agency, he returned to prison today, Thursday, 21 Aban. Khaki had been granted leave on 10 Aban.

Mark Rutte, NATO Secretary General, evaluated the Abu Dhabi talks positively and described the positions of the US, Europe, and Ukraine in these talks as very coordinated. However, Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine, described the US approach to talks with Russia about the new security order as "strange."

Washington police announced that in a shooting on Thursday morning inside a gym in the Logan Circle neighborhood, one person was killed and four were injured, one of whom is in critical condition. The suspect barricaded himself in an apartment on the seventh floor of a residential building and was found by police after about an hour with a self-inflicted gunshot wound and has died. The motive for the shooting is still unknown.

A video released on social media shows moments of the immortal dance of Behnam Kashani, a 33-year-old tattoo artist. He was killed on 18 Dey during protests in front of the intelligence building in Mahallat city, Markazi province, by gunfire from suppression forces.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation suspended Yaser Asani, Esteghlal winger, for two matches due to misconduct towards the referee in the match against Esteghlal Khuzestan, with one match suspended, and fined him 500 million tomans. Alireza Ildarom, the assistant referee, was suspended from refereeing for two months due to misconduct towards Asani. Esteghlal and Tractor clubs were each fined 500 million tomans due to fan behavior and spectator chants, and the return match between Tractor and Malavan will be played without spectators.

Mehr news agency on Thursday, 21 Aban 1405 reported a video from the sky of Tehran and announced that the Islamic Republic's armed forces tested "new missiles" in the west of Iran's capital. Received images from citizens show the launch of three missiles from the Bidganeh area.

Anita Anand, Canada's Foreign Minister, announced that Ottawa voted against the Islamic Republic's membership in the "Programme and Coordination Committee" in a secret vote at the UN General Assembly. Anand said the Islamic Republic suppresses opponents and fuels instability in the Middle East. She added that a government with such a record is not qualified to be a member of a body tasked with upholding the UN Charter.

According to rescuers, three wooden boats that arrived on Thursday, 21 Aban, at the port of La Restinga on El Hierro island, one of the Canary Islands of Spain, carried more than 150 migrants who had been at sea for nearly a week. Fernando Clavijo, head of the local government of the Canary Islands, announced that from 10 to 19 Aban, 7,432 migrants had entered these islands and warned about the increase in migration via the Atlantic route. Clavijo said authorities had previously received warnings and information about increased boat movements from West Africa.
Hamza Zia, an Iraqi journalist, published a video of Sardar Azmoun during the national football team training in Iraq and sarcastically wrote: "The training resistance band defeated Azmoun."

Masoud Pezeshkian said on Thursday, 21 Aban, after the UN Climate Change Summit in Antalya that countries claiming democracy and human rights have violated legal and human principles. He added that the summit was an opportunity to express the Islamic Republic's positions and to talk with presidents and prime ministers of other countries. Pezeshkian also met with Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Luis Inacio Lula da Silva, and the head of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.

At dawn on Wednesday, 20 Aban, the execution of a prisoner named Ebrahim Bezi, 42 years old and father of two children, was carried out in Gorgan prison. This prisoner had previously been sentenced to death for murder.

The process of repression and security control in Iranian schools has taken new dimensions in response to support for Prince Reza Pahlavi. A government cleric disguised as a "Pahlavi supporter" conducted ideological interrogations of young students. This action followed anti-government slogans and support for the Pahlavi family in schools and has caused insecurity among students and their families.

The Israeli Prime Minister's Office announced that a security meeting between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eizenkot ended after about two hours. Guy Markizno was also present at the meeting. Eizenkot was briefed on the current security and diplomatic challenges facing Israel, and both parties agreed to keep each other informed of developments if necessary.

The Prosecutor General and Revolutionary Prosecutor of Yazd province announced that a former member of the city council was arrested upon returning to the country due to what was described as "publishing content against national security in cyberspace." This individual was released from prison after a while on bail.
On Tuesday, 19 Aban, a contract worker employed at the Sina offshore drilling rig fell from a height into the sea while working and died.

Contract and subcontract workers at Abadeh Cement Factory in Fars province have reported wage arrears of three to seven months and problems with their insurance payments. These workers have asked officials to end their uncertainty.

Israel's Kan network reported on Thursday, 21 Aban, quoting a US official that US Central Command recently sent a message to Israeli military representatives in the US to prepare for the possibility of resuming war with Iran. Similar messages were sent to Israel and Gulf countries. The US continues to transfer equipment to the Middle East, with two aircraft carriers present in the region.

Videos received show a gathering of unsettled owners of Kooy Shahrara in Borujerd on 20 Aban. According to some victims, the lands of Kooy Shahrara were purchased in 1382 through a triple cooperative of the army, education department, and municipality from farmers, and land transfer documents were given to about five thousand members of these cooperatives, but the owners remain unsettled.

On Thursday, 21 Aban, garbage truck drivers in Tabriz stopped work and protested due to lack of social security insurance and non-payment of annual wage increases. Machine manufacturing workers in Tabriz went on strike in recent days over irregularities in salary payments. Additionally, a group of dismissed workers and unemployed youth in the city of Har and the Haft-Tappeh area protested unemployment in front of the Haft-Tappeh Sugarcane Company.

The execution of Ebrahim Bezi in Gorgan prison highlights again the risk of reproducing violence and a cycle of revenge in Iran's qisas system. It was reported that two tribes had reached a verbal agreement to pardon the qisas, but the execution was carried out, increasing the likelihood of new hostility. This situation reveals fundamental flaws in the qisas mechanism that transfers the moral responsibility of the death decision to families and can escalate violence.
The Domino audio version reports that JD Vance's mission in nuclear negotiations with Tehran has ended.

Ebrahim Asmani, a Turkic (Azerbaijani) activist, has been detained by security forces in Tabriz for 11 days and remains held in the Intelligence Department's detention center. According to Harana News Agency, he was arrested on Monday, 11 Aban.
IRNA, quoting official sources, reported that Sirik in Hormozgan province was hit by the "enemy" minutes ago. According to this report, the hit was of a military nature.

Iran International's investigation shows that Hossein Yazdankhah, a lesser-known judge at the Khorasan Revolutionary Court, has sentenced at least 11 detained protesters to death since the start of the nationwide protests in Dey 1404. He was also a member of the panel of judges issuing the death sentences for two other protesters who were recently executed.

Fars News Agency reported that residents of Sirik County in eastern Hormozgan Province heard several explosions in recent hours. Fars stated that the cause of these sounds is still unknown but suggested they might be warning shots fired at violating ships. IRNA, citing official sources, reported that Sirik was targeted in a military attack.

The newspaper L'Équipe reported that Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, is suspected of employing a woman without legal residency status in the US at his Miami home and then using his position to obtain a work permit for her. A complaint has been filed with the US tax authority requesting an investigation into the hiring and payment of this woman. FIFA denied the claim, stating Infantino personally pays the staff at his home.

A video published on social media shows a group of mothers seeking justice for the disappeared in Shiraz gathered beside the tomb of Payam Rakhbakhsh, one of the victims of the Dey protests, and they recited the names of their children.

Bernard Canten, Belgium's Minister of the Interior and Security, announced evidence suggesting that hacker groups linked to the Islamic Republic may have played a role in recent cyberattacks on cooling systems of supermarkets in the country. He said Belgian security services have obtained evidence of a possible connection to known Iranian agents, and the federal prosecutor's office is investigating. These attacks in early November disrupted cooling systems in several stores, forcing them to discard food worth tens of thousands of euros.

Lionel Scaloni agreed on Thursday to continue as head coach of the Argentina national football team until the end of the 2030 World Cup. This agreement ended speculation about his future following Argentina's defeat in this year's World Cup final. Scaloni had expressed doubts about continuing with the national team after Argentina's loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

Jonathan Sayegh, an analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said Washington is in no hurry to reach an agreement with the Islamic Republic after the midterm elections and that the status of "neither war nor peace" benefits Washington. He added that political legacy has become more important for Trump after the Republicans' defeat, and Washington should combine maximum pressure on the Islamic Republic with maximum support for the Iranian people.

The mother of Amirhossein Vandalvand, a 21-year-old who was killed by direct gunfire during the January 9 protests in Tehran, released a video on the tenth month of her son's death showing her seeing and smelling his clothes and said: "The weather has gotten cold, my son. Why don't you come anymore?"

Jaber Rajabi, a political analyst, said the request by the Assembly of Experts to review Iran's exit from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and change its defense doctrine reflects a power struggle between clerics and the Revolutionary Guards. He added that Iranian officials believe acquiring nuclear weapons could create deterrence, but such threats might backfire and increase the likelihood of military conflict.
In the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad, it was reported that Trump excluded Pence from negotiations with Iran.

Alireza Kiani discussed the Islamic Republic's claim of influencing the US midterm congressional elections on the program 19 "Fereydoun" and emphasized that the Republicans' defeat in this election can be explained based on the usual pattern of the incumbent president's party losing midterm elections.
A reporter asked if it would be a defeat for Trump if, after his presidency ends, the mad rulers in Iran remain in power. Trump replied yes, it would be a defeat. Definitely.

Harry Kane played his 126th international match in England's game against Croatia in the UEFA Nations League, surpassing Peter Shilton's record of 125 games to become the record holder for most international appearances in the history of England men's football. Before the match, Kane received a special jersey from Shilton and said the focus is on the team, not himself. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Kane deserved the 2026 Ballon d'Or and now breaks the national team record with 126 games.

Alireza Kiani said in program 19 "Fereydoun" that contrary to the perception of uniformity in the positions of the American right-wing, the reality is that, for example regarding the Middle East, the positions of the American right-wing are not uniform.

Halvash reported, citing local sources and public reports, that on Thursday evening several loud explosions and intense, continuous gunfire were heard in parts of Saravan County, Sistan and Baluchestan. The cause of these explosions and any possible casualties or damages are not yet known.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, in response to a question from Salem News about the consequences of the killing of a senior American official by the Islamic Republic, said: "It won't be long before they no longer exist."

Farzin Nadimi said the deployment of about 200 refueling aircraft and the presence of US aircraft carriers in the region provide the necessary capability for a severe military operation against the Islamic Republic. He added that these capabilities are sufficient to support US and Israeli airstrikes, but a large-scale war requires more bombers. Nadimi also said the Islamic Republic has missile capability to threaten US bases in the region, but attacks on US bases in Europe could escalate tensions, and extensive US attacks might reduce the Islamic Republic's ability to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Amir Giti, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that internal political developments in Israel and disputes over forming a new government will not prevent military action by the country against the Islamic Republic. He added that if Israeli officials conclude that their country's security is at risk, they might attack without Washington's approval. Giti also said that despite coordination between the Israeli army and the US Central Command, no decision has yet been made to start immediate military operations.

Shayan Samiei said that the Islamic Republic's warnings to South Korea and other countries present in the Strait of Hormuz are an effort to pressure US allies and prevent a possible military attack. He added that the Islamic Republic does not have the capacity for a broad confrontation with Washington's allies and wants to push regional countries to mediate. Samiei also said Tehran is seeking to buy time, and the contradictory positions of Islamic Republic officials indicate a serious challenge in accepting US conditions.

The Iran Human Rights Organization reported that Amir Salar Davoodi, a detained human rights lawyer, faces three security charges, including espionage for releasing an audio file of his clients' telephone wedding ceremony. Davoodi released the audio file on 12 Mehr, one day before the execution of his client Alireza Sepahi Badjani. Since his arrest on 19 Mehr, he has been held without any contact with the outside world, and his lawyer has not been allowed access to the case file.

Trump said in an interview with the Street Shooter podcast that he can immediately end the war with Iran but has allowed the current situation to continue at the request of regional countries including Saudi Arabia and the UAE. He said these Middle Eastern countries have invested trillions of dollars in the US and must be protected. Trump called the Islamic Republic an "empire of evil" and said Tehran is collapsing under Washington's continued pressure.

Trump said in an interview with Hugh Hewitt's podcast that if hardliners in Iran remain in power by the end of his presidency, it would be a failure for him. He listed the destruction of Iran's nuclear program among his presidential achievements and added that his administration's actions at the US border should also be included. Trump stated he would not hesitate to take military action again against the Iranian regime and is willing to continue the naval blockade.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed in a statement that in response to the US midnight airstrike on Sirik, it targeted and destroyed the US early warning radar in Bahrain. The statement said this is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC warned that if violations are repeated, its aerospace force is fully prepared for borderless confrontation.

Sadegh Beigdeli, a lawyer and international affairs expert, said that the limited attacks by the US on the Islamic Republic are part of assessing the capabilities and reactions of the parties. He emphasized that the naval blockade and increased economic pressure have started a silent war against the Islamic Republic, whose effects are gradually becoming clearer. Beigdeli also said that reduced economic growth, decreased investment, and increased poverty are consequences of these pressures, and the US does not necessarily need to enter a full-scale war to continue them.

After the collapse of a residential building in Brooklyn and the death of at least eight people, including two children, the mayor of New York expanded investigations to five companies related to the adjacent workshop and 100 other construction sites. Municipal records show the adjacent workshop had been subject to a work stoppage order months earlier.

Kamyar Baharang, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to the Assembly of Experts' statement about the possibility of the Islamic Republic leaving the NPT treaty and said this threat not only does not restore the regime's lost deterrence but could provide a pretext for expanding global consensus against the Islamic Republic. He also emphasized that threatening Arab countries and their infrastructures pushes these countries more than before to strengthen defense cooperation with the US and Israel and makes the prospect of any negotiations with the Islamic Republic more difficult.

Four labor and retirees' organizations jointly criticized the Islamic Republic government for opposing the increase of the minimum wage for workers, stating that wage increases over the past five decades have always been much lower than the inflation rate. Rouzbeh Boulahri explains why the Medical government lacks the will to raise the minimum wage for workers and other wage earners and what the outcome of this situation will be.

A Chilean mother finally met her two children who were taken from her during the military dictatorship after nearly four decades of separation. This meeting recalled the case of forced adoptions and child trafficking during Chile's military dictatorship, which led to the separation of about 25,000 children from their families.

The Wall Street Journal reported that hackers affiliated with the Iranian government have increased cyberattacks on infrastructure and internet-connected equipment by changing their operation methods. These attacks include three incidents from this summer targeting water facilities in the US, two oil tankers heading to Texas, and hundreds of store refrigerators in Europe. The newspaper identified hackers affiliated with the Iranian government as the main suspects in all three attacks.

The New York Times reported that the Islamic Republic seizes the assets and bank accounts of families of opponents and journalists abroad to pressure them. According to the report, assets of more than 400 Iranians abroad have been confiscated on charges of cooperating with hostile governments. Ardeshir Zarezadeh, a lawyer and human rights activist, explains the consequences of the expansion of asset seizures and economic pressure on the families of activists abroad and its impact on curbing critics of the Islamic Republic.

Omid Memarian, a political analyst, said the Islamic Republic is organizing cross-border actions to create intimidation and extend the atmosphere of repression outside Iran. He emphasized these actions aim to scare journalists and prevent them from media activities. Memarian added that host countries should prevent the continuation of this policy through international follow-up and increasing political costs.

Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, announced that the armed forces of the Islamic Republic have the capability to launch missiles with two-ton warheads at targets 1500 kilometers away. He stated that the purpose of this missile capability is to neutralize enemy plans to harm Iran's security and power. Izadi also said that the myth of security for American bases is over and that the Islamic Republic has shown that American imperialism is a paper tiger.

Mizan News Agency reported the indictment of six people in the case of the Fitex Tehran sports exhibition and the arrest of all six. The case has been referred to the Ethics Crimes Prosecutor's Office. The judiciary stated the charges include encouraging people to corruption and immorality and publishing obscene images on social media.

Naqi Shabaniyan, deputy of Tehran Parks Organization, said that currently 40 to 45 percent of the trees in Sarkheh Hesar Park have dried up and some trees are affected by varying degrees of dryness and pests. He cited old age, consecutive droughts, reduced irrigation, and Tehran's air pollution as factors of tree drying. He also said air pollution disrupts the gas exchange of leaves and various pests and diseases have damaged the trees.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic may have operational capability to damage US and European bases but this does not mean achieving victory. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic's actions have so far failed to create deterrence and that it is currently experiencing a period of collapse.

Iman Aghayari, a political analyst, said the Islamic Republic prioritizes confronting normative and behavioral changes in society even during economic and social crises. He emphasized that the government's insistence on imposing its desired lifestyle indicates the social failure of the Islamic Republic's policies. According to him, the government's priority is maintaining political dominance even if this approach imposes heavy costs on society.

A video released on social media shows the mother of Mohammad Jahandideh at the grave of Mehdi Jamshidi; the two mothers cried together. Mohammad Jahandideh, 23 years old, was killed on 19 Dey in Fardis, and Mehdi Jamshidi, 24 years old, died on the evening of 18 Dey 1404 in Rustamabad, Gilan.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that any hostile action by the enemy will be met with terrible and painful strikes. He said the enemy should learn from its successive defeats, otherwise greater lessons are on the way. Vahidi also declared that the revenge for the killing of Ali Khamenei, the former leader of the Islamic Republic, will be realized.

Bruno Fernandes, the captain of Manchester United, has rejected the club's second offer to extend his contract, leaving his future at Old Trafford uncertain. Negotiations to extend the contract of this 32-year-old midfielder continue due to disagreements over salary and contract length. Fernandes' contract ends in June 2027, and he can negotiate with other clubs from January, but Manchester United has the option to extend his contract for one year.

The French national team lost 3-1 to Italy at San Siro stadium, marking the first defeat under coach Zinedine Zidane. Experts and Zidane's close friends heavily criticized the team's performance, especially in the second half when players lacked fighting spirit. Late substitutions and playing inexperienced players were also criticized.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, and Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, held a two-hour meeting in Jerusalem to discuss Israel's security and diplomatic challenges. According to a joint statement, the two sides agreed to continue consultations and information exchange if needed.

A knowledgeable source told Iran International that Fatemeh Mokhtari, a 23-year-old woman and one of the detainees of the Dey protests, was sentenced to 10 years in prison by the Fifth Branch of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court after being arrested without a judicial warrant and enduring severe beatings during interrogations. The source added that the Fifth Branch of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, headed by Judge Vahid Hemmatnejad, sentenced Mokhtari on 9 Tir to 10 years in prison on various charges. Fatemeh Mokhtari has been in prison for more than six months.

An image received by Iran International shows that the relatives and family of Alireza Raeisi, a protester of the National Revolution of Dey month who was executed by the judiciary, held a 40th-day memorial ceremony at his grave under security pressures. Raeisi, 21 years old, was buried in the deserts of Anarak after his execution in Mehr month and in the Dastgerd prison of Isfahan.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi, advisor to the commander of the IRGC, stated that the people will not accept anything but revenge for the leader's blood. He said that the demand for revenge is the public's desire and that this issue is not new and will continue. Naqdi added that this matter will not end without revenge against the leader's killers and that this revenge will be taken.

A member of the honor guard fainted on Wednesday, 20 Aban, simultaneously with the arrival of Peter Pellegrini, President of Slovakia, at the Élysée Palace in Paris to meet Emmanuel Macron, President of France.

On the birthday of Ali Jafari, a video was published on social media showing that his birthday cake was placed on his tombstone. Ali, 31 years old, was killed by a direct gunshot on 19 Dey 1404 in Saein Qaleh, Zanjan.

The International Atomic Energy Agency warned in its confidential report that the lack of information about Iran's enriched uranium stocks and lack of access to nuclear facilities has created serious concerns about nuclear weapons proliferation. The agency stated that since the June 2025 attacks, except for the Bushehr power plant, it has not received information about the status of facilities and nuclear materials nor had access to them. The agency's director general called for the immediate resumption of verification activities.

Saeed Shakiba, a blogger and satirist imprisoned in Tehran's central prison, was sentenced to five years in prison by Branch 28 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court for releasing a video imitating the voice of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The sentence was communicated to him on Wednesday, 20 Aban. He was convicted on charges of assembly and collusion.

The Public Relations of the Navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that a ship collided with a naval mine after ignoring repeated warnings and attempting to pass through an unauthorized and dangerous route. The IRGC said that this ship was supported by American fighter jets for passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international relations analyst, said Donald Trump's statements about his defeat if the Islamic Republic survives until the end of his presidency show that the Iran issue has become a matter of prestige for him. According to Alizadeh, Trump wants to resolve this issue in the remaining two years of his presidency, but he has not yet made a clear decision about military action or continuing economic pressure.

The French Blood Transfusion Organization announced that judicial investigations have started regarding a cyberattack on cooling systems of blood product storage centers. The attack occurred on the night of November 1 to 2, altering temperature and defrosting settings of equipment. The organization cannot comment on the details due to ongoing investigations.

Amid the worsening economic crisis and livelihood problems, unpaid salaries and insurance claims are among the issues reported by citizens. Emergency 115 staff say they have not received bonuses for one year, and employees of Parsian Trading Company in Isfahan report unpaid salaries for the past three months.

The Israeli army announced that Kurt Renshaw, commander of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, during his visit to Israel, met with Eyal Harel, commander of the Israeli Navy, and other senior naval officials to discuss strengthening naval cooperation and maritime security. The meeting took place on 21 Aban at the end of Renshaw's visit to Israel. The two sides discussed Israeli naval operations, cooperation to maintain regional stability, and exchange of knowledge and technology.

A widespread disruption in Microsoft's cloud infrastructure has prevented millions of users from accessing the company's systems and software, and has also affected companies like OpenAI. Microsoft says this disruption is not caused by a cyberattack.

With the continuation of disciplinary and judicial rulings against students, Fariborz Kohanzad, a student at Sharif University of Technology in Tehran who had raised the Lion and Sun flag of Iran during the National Revolution university protests last year, announced his expulsion from the university. He announced this news by posting a picture and a post on the X network.

A layer of air pollution has spread over Tehran, covering parts of the city in a haze of smoke and dust. This situation is clearly visible from the summit of Tochal. The accumulated pollution volume depicts the air quality status of Tehran.

The International Atomic Energy Agency expressed concern about the underground uranium enrichment facilities in Isfahan, which inspectors have not yet accessed. The agency stated in a confidential report that it lacks precise information about the location of the facilities, the monitoring status, and the possible presence of nuclear materials at the site.

Amin Oveis-Gharani, a political prisoner, is serving his sentence in Semnan prison. He was sentenced to seven years in prison by the First Branch of the Semnan Revolutionary Court. This news was confirmed by an informed source close to Oveis-Gharani's family to the HRANA news agency.
Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said senior Israeli army commanders consider concerns about an Iranian attack to be unfounded and believe Israel should not enter a military campaign alone.

Mohammad Baqer Mohammadi Laeini, the Friday prayer leader of Sari, said in the Friday prayers on 12 Aban that Iran's missile range has no limits and any American base in Europe and beyond can be targeted. He added that people demand a review of the defense doctrine and consideration of leaving the NPT. He also emphasized that geographical limitations in defense have been removed and any place necessary will be targeted.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International while driving, showing that his car's fuel was running out. He expressed concern about being stranded in the desert and said, "Even if a pump is available at night in Sistan and Baluchestan, there is no gasoline."

It was reported that Amir Radmanmehr was shot and killed by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic's suppression in Vali Asr town of Isfahan on 19 Dey. It was said that his name will remain in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, said that hijablessness is becoming a custom in the country and the principle of hijab is disappearing. He added that hijablessness is illegal and government bodies must fight it. Alamolhoda also said the enemy wants to distance society from its Fatimid identity through cultural dominance.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said Donald Trump has no way to end the threats from the Islamic Republic except by ending the regime's existence. He added that the Islamic Republic aims to dominate the Strait of Hormuz and push the US out of the region, goals that conflict with the security strategy of the US and its allies. Ghazizadeh also said the Islamic Republic views economic blockade as equivalent to war, and the US, Europe, and regional countries must bear the cost of major changes in the Middle East.

Emmanuel Macron, the President of France, has expressed readiness to support Arsène Wenger's potential candidacy in the FIFA presidential election and has offered to negotiate with leaders of various countries to secure votes for him. The deadline for registering candidates for the FIFA presidential election ends on November 18. Some sources have warned about Macron's role, stating that France's tense relations with several African countries may complicate efforts to gain votes from federations on that continent.

It was reported that the home of Tara Moghimi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Hamedan, was searched by intelligence officers on Sunday, 26 Mehr. During this search, some of her personal belongings were confiscated. She was summoned to the Hamedan intelligence office, interrogated, and then released.

Esmaeil Saghab Esfahani, Vice President, says the free gasoline price, currently 10,000 tomans per liter, is reviewed every season based on government approval. He added that changing this price depends on the purchase price of gasoline from refineries. Reports have also emerged of long queues at fuel stations and restricted access to fuel cards in 11 provinces.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that they received a three million toman voucher for a family of three but had to pay extra out of pocket for buying rice and eggs.

New information received by Iran International indicates the role of security officials, including the protection officers of the Imam Jumu'ah office in Qorveh, in suppressing people and shooting protesters. Mohsen Mahimini discusses the protests in Kurdistan province in January in the Geography of the Iranian National Revolution program.

Adam Bailey, spokesperson for Iran International, reacted to the conviction of Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi-Mansh in a spying case against the network's journalists by warning that the court ruling does not mean the end of threats against journalists. Bailey praised the efforts of the British police to protect the network's staff. The Committee to Protect Journalists also welcomed the conviction of the two Iranians and said the court evidence shows how far the Islamic Republic is willing to go to silence journalists.

Esteghlal Club protested the disciplinary committee's ruling regarding Yaser Asani and requested an investigation into the assistant referee's alleged insult to the player. Esteghlal announced it will appeal the issued ruling to the appeals committee. The club also demanded a review of evidence and the assistant referee's statements, emphasizing that justice must be applied equally to all.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, wrote in a note to Japan's Kyodo News that the United States has legal responsibility for military attacks on Iran and must stop these attacks, guarantee they will not recur, and compensate for all damages. Araghchi called the US and Israeli attacks a clear violation of international law and said the US attack was carried out without UN Security Council authorization. He also emphasized that the Islamic Republic has the right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

Ahmad Motahari-Asl, the Friday prayer leader of Tabriz, said in the city's Friday prayers that God hears the voices of the oppressed and will respond to oppressors at the right time, and God willing, the US will be expelled from the region and Israel will be destroyed. He added that changes in personnel and power shifts in the US do not change the nature of its policies. Motahari-Asl also said that expelling the US and destroying Israel are demands of Muslim nations and the crimes of oppressors will not go unanswered.

Manchester United announced that Mauricio Pochettino, the Argentine coach of the US national team, will take charge of the club from November 18. Manchester United confirmed that they have reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Pochettino and his staff's departure. Pochettino has coached teams like Tottenham and Paris Saint-Germain and led the US national team to the round of 16 in the World Cup.

A video shows that the mother of Mahdi Zarei showered the place where her son was killed with flowers and kissed it. Mahdi, 22 years old, was targeted in the protests on 18 Dey 1404 in Haft-Hoz, Tehran.

Mostafa Pourdehghan, a member of the Parliament's Industry and Mines Commission, said that the gap between incomes and expenses is increasing day by day in the current economic conditions and that Iran's economy is severely deteriorating. He added that various income deciles and percentiles mostly struggle with relative poverty and their economic conditions are very bad. Pourdehghan also said that poverty drives people to first give up welfare needs and then prioritize between health and eating.

Reza (Abdolreza) Amani Far, Asghar Hajeb, and Roghieh Torabpour, members of the Bushehr Teachers' Trade Union, were sentenced to a total of 12 years, six months, and one day of imprisonment and additional punishments.

Hamid Estili, a veteran Iranian footballer, said about the neglect of the Islamic Republic anthem at the farewell ceremony for Hamid Alidousti that every place is for a specific purpose and the anthem should not be played at that ceremony; instead, the Quran should be played.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, on Friday, 22 Aban, denied the IRGC's claim about an attack on a US early warning radar in Bahrain, stating that no radar was damaged in the attack. CENTCOM emphasized that the IRGC launched two suicide drones towards Bahrain early Friday, both of which were shot down by US forces. The IRGC public relations had announced that the Aerospace Force targeted and destroyed a US early warning radar in Bahrain.

Reports indicate intensified disciplinary and judicial actions against students and increased security controls and government propaganda in schools. There are reports of expulsion of protesting students and political interrogations of pupils. This occurs simultaneously with ongoing crackdowns after the Iranian National Revolution.

Ata Hosseinian, an economic and energy journalist, said the quota for 3,000-toman gasoline has been halved and the third rate has reached 10,000 tomans per liter. He added that the government, by limiting access to gasoline at stations and with reports of gasoline being sold at 103,000 to 110,000 tomans per liter, is preparing the ground for accepting a rate of 70,000 to 80,000 tomans to earn more revenue.
